thread:
sam: Heads up — noticed a ~28% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for redwood-v2 on /chat/completion since the kernel batching patch landed yesterday. Token-saved/sec down ~2.1M for the cluster.

jia: Ack. Any tenant-level spikes or is it global?

sam: Mostly concentrated on a few high-volume tenants (AcmeCorp, BlueBird). Per-route breakdown shows /chat/completion and /summarize leading. Per-model heatmap attached in dashboard but I pasted quick numbers: redwood-v2: 62% -> 45% overall. redwood-quant: 71% -> 68% (small).

omar: Interesting — I profiled warmup path and saw that the batching heuristic now trims trailing whitespace differently which changes the cache key normalization for multi-turn prompts. Could be key variance.

maya: If key normalization drifted, that would explain tenant-specific drops if they use more assistant style prompts. Any examples?

omar: Example diff: old normalizer kept trailing newlines for multi-shot blocks, new one strips them in batching stage. Key derivation is `sha256(prefix + normalized_suffix)` so small change flips keys.

sam: Ugh. So this is a functional regression, not model change. Can we detect where the mismatch happens upstream? Maybe add a small histogram of `normalized_len_diff` by route.

jia: I pushed a quick grafana panel suggestion: heatmap of key_entropy vs hit_rate per model+route, and a tenant waterfall for token-saved delta. Also added an alert: if %hit drop > 10% for a model-route over 30m, page on-call. Thoughts? :warning:

maya: Good. We should also add a metric for "key_transform_version" tag so we can see where requests were normalized by old vs new code. Fastest fix is to revert the normalization change in the batching layer.

sam: Can we rollback the batching normalization without losing the batching perf gains? We need a mitigation that keeps throughput.

omar: I can change the normalizer to emit a canonicalized key that strips vs preserves in a stable way and keep batching behavior untouched — basically normalize at key-derivation layer instead of at batch-assembly. That keeps kernels intact. I'll open a PR.

sam: Please also add a short-lived dashboard panel that shows (per-tenant) "tokens_saved_hourly" and cumulative daily $impact — finance wants a quick estimate. Example PromQL I used to get token-saved per tenant: 

```
sum by (tenant) (increase(prefix_cache_tokens_saved_total[1h]))
```

maya: For observability, we should instrument: `key_version` label, `normalized_length`, and `key_collision_rate` (ratio of collisions per 1M keys). Add a tiny histogram for normalized_length to detect sudden mass shifts.

jia: Agreed. Also, add a per-model "estimated token-cost-saved" panel: tokens_saved * avg_cost_per_token(model). I put a placeholder multiplier for now.

infra-bot: deploybot: Batch-normalizer v2 rolled out to eng-runtime cluster at 3612345600 — can revert with `deploy rollback batch-normalizer v2`

sam: Thanks infra-bot. Omar — priority: PR to move normalization into key-derivation (safe), plus dashboard patches. Target: hotfix today. Maya — can you draft the alert thresholds and a runbook? I'll collect tenant owners for short-term warmup prefetch for the top-3 affected tenants.

omar: On it. I'll add the `key_version` tag and emit both old/new keys for 24h to measure mapping rate.

maya: Drafting runbook now: include rollback steps, query to list affected tenants, and cost-estimate calc. Putting in #oncall-docs after review.

sam: If we need an immediate stopgap: enable per-tenant prefix-warmup for AcmeCorp and BlueBird for 6 hours. Low risk and should restore token-saved quickly.

jia: I'll add that to the console: canary warmup + short TTL (6h) so it doesn't drift. Also creating the heatmap panel: path `Observability / PrefixCache / Explainability` with tabs: model, route, tenant, token-saved waterfall.

sam: Great. Assigning follow-ups: omar -> PR (normalize-at-key), jia -> dashboard + alert, maya -> runbook, sam -> tenant outreach. Update here when PR/alert/dash pushed. :thumbsup:

omar: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4587 (norm at key-derivation). Includes tests for both formats and a migration toggle.

jia: Dashboard patched, alert rule pushed (testing prod:mute). Panel shows immediate correlation between new key_version=2 and hit drop.

maya: Runbook in #oncall-docs, link: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/prefix-cache-hitrate-regression. Includes rollback command and cost calc.

sam: Rolling warmup for AcmeCorp/BlueBird now. Monitoring token-saved.

sam: Update: after warmup tokens_saved/sec recovered ~70% for AcmeCorp, entire cluster improved ~12% in hit-rate. Still below pre-patch by ~10% pending PR.

omar: Merged and rolled out fix at 3612345800. We'll keep `key_version` for 48h and then remove legacy mapping after no mismatches.

sam: Nice. Closing loop later with a postmortem note and adding a permanent dashboard tile for key_version and normalized_len distribution.

maya: + add a weekly job that samples tenant key stability and alerts if drift > 5%.

sam: Thanks all.
